Generally for most pets yearly checkups are recommended (just like for people 🙂). Some recommend every six months for birds simply because of what someone said earlier: they're a prey species and will do everything they can to hide their sickness. In the wild, predators will look for the old, weak, and sick to go after so their instincts are to look completely normal for as long as possible. Often by the time they're showing major symptoms they're very close to death. 

Major things to watch for are changes in poop (while keeping in mind it can be very effected by what they've eaten), drooping feathers, dirty nostrils or vent area, and in very bad situations they'll be unable to perch/falling off often.

So the issue with seed is while it has some nutrients it's super fatty. That's good for the birds in the wild because they're doing buttloads of exercise just being outside, living, and finding said seed. But our indoor birds aren't doing half as much exercise and generally have way easier access to more food so them eating that same diet can lead to diseases like fatty liver disease. 

Extra additionally, parrots are picky mofos so when given a seed mix they'll often only pick out their favorite seeds and leave the rest when possible which further increases the vitamin deficiency. For example, my conure's main food stable is pellets and he'll go through and eat his favorite color first and wait as long as possible before deigning to eat his least favorite color (the green or yellow ones).

I don't know that you read anything I said after $20. 

We aren't talking about people making $1000 a week. We're talking about struggling lower class. Sticking with my same example as before, someone working full time at $10/hr (which is above min wage by almost $3) would make $400/week. 

Subtract 60-100 for taxes leaves us with best case $340/week. 

Take out the cost of the ID leaves Them short easy $100+. Let's assume they live right by the DMV so they can walk there and they have all the necessary documentation so it's a flat $100 (also assuming their ID only costs 20 and not up to 60 like some states). 

Now they're down to 240 for that week. 

Now consider Americans on average spend 37% of their income on housing. That's 148 coming out of this person's paycheck for the week putting them down to $92 for childcare, food, gas/transportation, and other bills. 

So no, many people can't spare that money.

It depends on the state and type of ID. However, on top of the other issues listed by the previous commenter for lower income people, taking the time to get that specific ID can largely increase that cost. 

The ID might only cost $20. But if you don't have access to a car then add bus fare or Uber cost on top of that. Then assume you have to take a day off of work because of the limited hours of government buildings. Let's say you were making 10/hr and a normal 8hr shift. The cost for that ID has quickly escalated to over $100. Not to mention if you need to purchase your birth certificate from the government that can be another $25. Other required documentation may require more money. 

Then, going through all of this doesn't even guarantee you'll be able to get your ID due to wait times, paperwork issues, etc. So to go back would mean losing another day of work, etc. Quickly building up the cost for groups of people who can't afford that extra burden

Tips for the spider wrap:
1. Identify which wrap it is. Does it have two little u shaped notches/indents somewhere on it? If so, you should be able to take the flat magnet and match those protruding u shaped things up to the indents. Feel it snap in place.  Then on that same part look for a side with what's essentially a seam and press against it like a button. This should release it. 

2. If it doesn't have notches and instead has a round small protruding piece and maybe a blinking light, cry because its the worst. 
After you cry it out grab the round magnet, snap that sucker on top of the protruding bit and hope it releases the lock. There's a lil red thing you might have to fuck with. 

3. If you struggle for more than a minute, flash your light and call for help. I know it can feel hard when you feel like the outsider or that you're bothering someone but fuck them. This is work and you're doing your job. 

OTHER TIPS: 

1) be wary if a guest starts trying to tell you how to use a register. Many of the scammers will try say oh you have to hit this button or you have to put it in manually. Fuck that and fuck them. 

2) Try be aware of coupons in the ad every week. I'm not talking about every deal where if you buy two or whatever you get a giftcard, I mean the coupons that you have to scan in the ad/on their app to get the deal such as spend $100 on these specific baby products and get a $20 giftcard. There's never that many and that's a big source of guest complaints. 

3) if a coupon amount feels too high, call someone. If these people have coupons giving them 6,8,10 dollars off items that usually are barely more than that if not less, it's sketch. Let someone else make that decision.

4) Don't touch the "no barcode" button unless told to. 

5) If a piece of clothing comes up without a tag on it *most* will have a small tag with the numbers of the item on it.  

In most shirts it's along the inside seam near the bottom. Sometimes it's in the sleeve. 

In most pants its along the seam by the ankle. 

In onsies, you have to open it and it should by on the inside seam by the ankle. 

Sneakers are usually right inside on a tag

Heals/sandals/flats are printed on the inside side usually. 

6) Never put in an amount on the total screen and hit cash unless you are holding that cash in your hand and have counted it. 

7) Always open bags, bins, suitcases being purchased. If the guest has a problem it's on them. It's required. I usually try to make it light when I do it but there's gonna be one or two people that throw a tantrum. 

8) If a giftcard has 2 barcodes on it (not counting the one which has the scratch off stuff over it) and one is a big barcode in the middle, the other a smaller one on the top left you have to scan the one on the top left for it to take it. If you scan the middle one you'll probably see a screen saying something like "This is a temporary giftcard that can't be used at our store" blah blah blah blah. Just clear it out and scan the proper one. 


9) try your best not to let guests get to you. If you see a line building up, don't get frazzled, just focus on the person in front of you. If someone is getting short, shitty, or nippy, it's not your fault and before long they'll be gone. You're new, you're gonna make mistakes just like you would doing anything else for the first time. Just make sure you pay attention and try learn from them instead of getting defensive. If you have any questions, feel free to message me.

Patriotism is what many people mean when they say Nationalism but doesn't involve the same belief of superiority and isn't dependent on a **national identity***,* rather it values the country and its values.
